envelope.text: group-taking verb reads as the node default

why:
same shape as `cpp:CallbackGroup::CallbackGroup`: ours takes the group NAME, rclcpp's takes the concurrency type and the auto-add flag. rclcpp's `CallbackGroupType` is a CONCURRENCY policy -- `MutuallyExclusive` or `Reentrant` -- and it only means anything to a multi-threaded executor deciding whether two callbacks from one group may run at once. RFC-0002 puts one executor on one RTOS task with non-preemptive run-to-completion dispatch, so every group is mutually exclusive by construction and `Reentrant` is unrepresentable: there is no second thread to be reentrant from. The axis our group carries instead is a NAME that `system.toml` maps to a scheduling tier (RFC-0047, RFC-0079) -- the thing a mixed-criticality image actually needs from grouping. `automatically_add_to_executor_with_node` (rclcpp's second constructor argument) is meaningless for the same reason as `cpp:Executor::add_node`. OUR LANGUAGES DISAGREE: RFC-0047 promised ONE mechanism across the three languages and shipped three. C++ has a `CallbackGroup` token type and `Node::create_callback_group`; C has no group type and no creation call at all -- the group is a bare `const char*` passed to `rclc_executor_add_subscription_in_group` / `_add_timer_in_group`, and ONLY those two entity kinds (a C service, client or action server cannot be put in a group); Rust has a sticky mode, `DeclaredNode::callback_group(&str)`, that labels every entity declared after it. Three spellings, and C's is missing capability rather than only a name.

phase-488 W3 (2026-10-25) -- upstream's overload ADDED beside ours, BOUNDED: `create_callback_group(rclcpp::CallbackGroupType, bool automatically_add = true)` returns `CallbackGroup::SharedPtr`, a `CallbackGroupToken` that converts to the null group every verb reads as the node default (`create_wall_timer`, `SubscriptionOptions::callback_group`, `create_service`'s trailing group). The name-taking overload still makes the tier-mapped NAMED group, which the token cannot hold, so a named group cannot be lost through it. Runtime: `ament_port_surface_runtime.cpp`.
